_timing: No narration yet. Each beat is the larger of the time it needs to finish animating and the time it takes to read, plus a 22-frame hold. This is a floor, not considered pacing — measure a real read and switch this topic to voiceCuts.

beats.text: Its most famous test picture came from a magazine.
beats.note: The Lenna image was cropped from the November 1972 issue of Playboy.

beats.text: A lab had run out of test images.
beats.note: Researchers at the University of Southern California wanted a human face, rich textures and a glossy finish.

beats.context: The width and height of the scan. It was made from the top 5.12 inches of the page, which was all the scanner could fit.

beats.note: The model, Lena Forsen, asked for it so the name would be pronounced correctly.

beats.text: Nature journals and IEEE have since turned it away.
beats.note: Decades of compression and vision papers used the same crop.

beats.text: A scanner's width fixed the size of an entire field's test image.

beats.line: Tech history is full of accidents.
